items.name: A1 Leg collar + thrust bulkhead + gimbal towers
items.why: The backbone. The four leg pods, the thrust bulkhead that carries all of the motor's thrust into the spine, and the two towers the gimbal pivots on are one part, so there are no joints to loosen in a crash.
partNames: A1 - Leg Collar + Thrust Bulkhead + Gimbal Towers [PAHT-CF]

items.name: A2 Avionics sled
items.why: Carries the Pixhawk on the front and the ESC on the back, clamped to both spine rods with split clamps so it can slide to trim the CG.

items.name: A3 Battery sled + quick-swap dock
items.why: Holds the battery module in two grooved rails (click in, pull out) and has a 20 × 20 mm M3 accessory port on the back for a logger or engine-sensor board later.

items.name: A6 SVPDB + PM02 tray
items.why: Mounts the servo BEC and the power module and holds the XT60 the battery module plugs into. ASA because it touches bare board pads.

items.name: A7 SVPDB + PM02 lid
items.why: Closes the power tray and traps the PM02 and SVPDB so vibration can't walk them loose.

items.name: G2 Gimbal servo frame
items.why: The pitch stage of the two-axis gimbal. It pivots in the A1 towers on shoulder screws and carries the roll servo.

items.name: G3 Gimbal motor bracket
items.why: The roll stage. The motor bolts straight to it, so the thrust vector is steered by tilting this bracket.
items.note: Being redesigned for the Himax CR2816 bolt pattern (4 × 3.5 mm on Ø43).

items.name: S1 Fairing, lower body
items.why: Lower fairing section, keyed onto the collar and held by two radial screws.

items.name: S2 Fairing, upper body + battery bay
items.why: Holds the whole battery bay opening and the 12 cooling slots that pull air past the ESC and pack.
partNames: S2 - Fairing - Upper Body (glue to S1 + S3) [ASA]

items.name: S3 Fairing, nose
items.why: Nose cone. Guides the tether line out of the top.

items.name: B-M1 Battery module shell
items.why: Wraps the LiPo so it slides into the dock as one unit. Flame-retardant because it touches the pack.

items.name: B-M2 Battery module back plate
items.why: Closes the module and traps the XT60 collar so the connector blind-mates when the module clicks in.
partNames: B-M2 - Battery module back plate + collar keeper [PC FR]

items.name: B-M3 XT60-F float collar
items.why: Epoxied onto the pack's XT60 so it can float about 0.5 mm and self-align with the vehicle-side connector.
partNames: B-M3 - XT60-F float collar (epoxy to the XT60-F) [PC FR]

items.name: B-M4 Battery latch + eject lever
items.why: Springy tongue with two hooks: it clicks the module in and levers it out. Nylon for fatigue life.
partNames: B-M4 - Battery latch + eject lever (print on its side) [PAHT-CF]

items.name: A5c PneuFoot (×4 + 2 spares)
items.why: Air-spring landing foot with a bleed jet: it soaks up the touchdown instead of bouncing.
partNames: A5c - PneuFoot (sole down, no supports) [TPU 95A HF]

items.name: A5 Lightweight TPU foot (×4 + 2 spares)
items.why: Simple TPU boot. 68 g lighter than the PneuFeet in total, so it's the foot for the first tethered hovers.

items.name: T1 Rod-top tether caps (×2)
items.why: With the fairing off, the tether bridle runs out of the open spine-rod tops through these caps.
partNames: T1 - Rod-top tether cap (hover-test build only) [PAHT-CF]

items.name: T2 Battery retainer strap
items.why: With no fairing wall for the latch to hook on, this TPU strap holds the battery module in.
partNames: T2 - Battery retainer strap (hover-test build only) [TPU 95A HF]

items.name: N1 Nav tray (GNSS + Wi-Fi bridge)
items.why: Carries the Wi-Fi MAVLink bridge and the RTK GNSS at the top of the vehicle, clear of the carbon.
partNames: N1 - Nav tray- RTK GNSS + Wi-Fi bridge [ASA]

items.name: N2 GNSS clamp bar
items.why: Clamps the helical GNSS antenna/receiver onto the nav tray.

items.name: N3 Wi-Fi bridge gate
items.why: Retains the XIAO board; remove it to reach the USB-C port for flashing.

items.name: N4 MTF-01 leg clamp
items.why: Clamps the optical-flow/ToF sensor to a leg, looking straight down, with a guard over the lenses.

items.name: N5 MTF-01 cable clips (×3)
items.why: Snap-on clips that run the sensor cable along the leg, so no leg drilling is needed.

items.name: C2 Carbon legs (×4, 235 mm)

PAHT-CF.name: Bambu Lab PAHT-CF (black)
PAHT-CF.why: Carbon-fibre nylon: the toughest stiff filament Bambu makes, 194 °C HDT next to the motor and ESC, and nylon clamps don't crack when tightened.
PAHT-CF.settings: Dry 80 °C 8–12 h. Hardened 0.4 nozzle, heated chamber, 5–6 walls, 40 % gyroid, 100 % infill in a 3 mm ring around each insert. PA/PET support interface.

ASA.name: Bambu Lab ASA (black)
ASA.why: Light, UV-stable and RF-transparent, so it can sit on bare board pads and under the GNSS and Wi-Fi antennas.
ASA.settings: Heated chamber (it warps otherwise), 3 walls on the 1.2 mm fairing skin, small brim. Joints weld with acetone.

PC FR.name: Bambu Lab PC FR (white; black was sold out)
PC FR.why: UL 94 V-0 flame-retardant polycarbonate for the parts that wrap the LiPo. Tough and slides well in the nylon dock.
PC FR.settings: Dry 80 °C 8 h. Heated chamber, glue stick, 4 walls, 25 % gyroid, brim on B-M1. Needs a full AMS (not AMS lite).

TPU 95A HF.name: Bambu Lab TPU 95A HF (black)
TPU 95A HF.why: Soft parts: feet, strap and clips. HF prints about 3× faster than normal TPU and stays airtight for the PneuFoot.
TPU 95A HF.settings: Dry 70 °C 8 h. 0.2 mm layers; PneuFoot 4 walls, 0 % infill, flow ≈ 1.05, seam outboard, sole down, no supports.

Support.name: Bambu Lab Support for PA/PET
Support.why: Break-away interface layer for the PAHT-CF parts (second H2D nozzle), so sockets and clamp faces come off clean.
